feat: Micro-ESPectre - Pure Python motion detection for MicroPython

Lightweight Python port of ESPectre for MicroPython with esp32-microcsi module.

Implementation:

- MVS segmentation algorithm aligned with C version
- Spatial turbulence with configurable subcarrier selection
- JSON-based config persistence (auto-save/load)
- MQTT Commands (backward compatibility with ESPectre)

refactor: remove unused K_FACTOR parameter

The k_factor parameter was originally intended as a threshold sensitivity
multiplier (effective_threshold = threshold * k_factor) to allow adjusting
detection sensitivity without changing the base threshold value.

Since adjusting the threshold value directly achieves the same result with simpler
configuration, k_factor is redundant and has been removed.

This simplifies the configuration interface: users can now directly adjust
the threshold value instead of managing two separate parameters.

feat: Increase traffic generator max rate to 1000 pps (Nyquist-Shannon theorem)

Increase maximum traffic generator rate from 50 to 1000 packets per second
to support high-frequency motion detection scenarios.

Rationale (Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem):
- For fast motion detection/precision localization (Fmax ≈ 300-400 Hz)
- Required sampling rate: Fs ≥ 2 × Fmax ≈ 600-1000 Hz
- Previous limit (50 pps) only supported vital signs monitoring
- New limit (1000 pps) enables full spectrum of Wi-Fi sensing applications

Changes:
- ESP32 (C): Centralized constants in traffic_generator.h
  * TRAFFIC_RATE_MIN = 0, TRAFFIC_RATE_MAX = 1000
  * Updated validation in traffic_generator.c and mqtt_commands.c
  * Fixed unsigned comparison warnings (removed < 0 checks)

- MicroPython: Centralized constants in config.py
  * TRAFFIC_RATE_MIN = 0, TRAFFIC_RATE_MAX = 1000
  * Updated traffic_generator.py and mqtt/commands.py
  * Default rate increased to 100 pps (was 20 pps)

Application Scenarios:
- Vital signs (breathing, heartbeat): 10-30 Hz (Low)
- Activity recognition (walking, sitting): 60-100 Hz (Medium)
- Fast motion/precision localization: 600-1000 Hz (High)

All validation logic and error messages updated to reflect new limits.

- Created espectre.h (formerly espectre_config.h) with all system constants

- Similar approach to Python's config.py

Simplified segmentation. Removed redundant:
- min_length
- max_length
- k_factor parameter

Validation Module:
- Created validation.h/c with centralized validation functions
- Implements 'validate at boundary' pattern (MQTT) + defensive validation (NVS)
- nvs_storage.c: Uses centralized validation with auto-fix
- segmentation.c: Removed validation from setters (trust caller)
- mqtt_commands.c: Uses centralized validate_float()

NVS Persistence Fixes:
- Fixed hardcoded values throughout codebase
- Proper NVS save/load for all configuration parameters
- Consistent parameter handling across modules

fix: Improve traffic generator resilience during SPIFFS operations

can occur during NBVI calibration when SPIFFS writes compete with

The errno:12 errors during calibration were already addressed in
85410f7, but these additional optimizations improve stability on
ESP32-S3 where PSRAM, SPIFFS, and WiFi compete for bus access.

This prevents the issue where calibration failure caused 2000%+ motion

fix: disable SerialStreamer when logger uses hardware UART

When ESPHome is configured with hardware_uart: UART0 (common on boards
with external USB-UART chips like CH343), the USB Serial JTAG driver
is not initialized. Calling usb_serial_jtag_read_bytes() in this case
causes a crash (Guru Meditation Error: Load access fault).

This fix checks for USE_LOGGER_USB_SERIAL_JTAG before enabling the
SerialStreamer. If the logger is not using USB Serial JTAG, the

feat: add ping mode for traffic generator

Add traffic_generator_mode option (dns/ping) to provide an alternative
when DNS queries don't work with certain routers.

- dns (default): UDP DNS queries to gateway:53
- ping: ICMP echo requests using ESP-IDF esp_ping API

Ping mode uses minimal 8-byte ICMP packets (header only, no payload).
Some routers don't respond to root domain DNS queries, causing low CSI
packet rates. Ping mode provides a fallback for these cases.

Updated documentation with packet size comparison table and airtime
calculations for both modes.

feat: add configurable gain lock mode with auto-skip for strong signals

Add gain_lock YAML option with three modes:
- auto (default): lock gain but skip if AGC < 30 (signal too strong)
- enabled: always force gain lock
- disabled: never lock gain

When ESP32 is too close to the AP (RSSI > -40 dB), forcing gain lock with
very low AGC values can freeze CSI reception. In auto mode, gain lock is
skipped with a warning instead of freezing the system.
